verified_bottleneck: On real camera in isolated driver/tracker probe, SDK get_capture wait is about 0.003 ms while enqueue_capture often takes 30-42 ms; capture consumption about 24-25 Hz. Current enqueue_capture uses the SDK infinite timeout, serializing RGB/depth publication behind tracker admission.
proposed_change: Use zero-timeout enqueue; skip only tracker submission on SDK TIMEOUT, preserve existing exception/fatal handling on SDK FAILED. Keep successful queue accounting, original body-result timestamps and all freshness/invalidity policies. Requires user decision; not implemented.
limits: Live full CRA FPS improvement and original intermittent missing synchronized captures remain unproven
A 60-second isolated real-camera test did not reproduce capture loss
Headless preview bypasses only GUI display functions and uses synthetic images; interactive render speed is not established
Reduced JPEG preview can differ slightly in pixels from full-decode/bilinear resize, with same output size; original images and body geometry are unchanged
No timeout extension, human-safety relaxation, GPU/model/FPS/resolution or smoothing change
proposal_tradeoffs: RGB/depth publication can proceed while SDK tracker input queue is busy
Body tracker inference throughput is not increased; some tracker inputs may be skipped
Faster depth reception versus delayed body-index/skeleton results can exceed the unchanged 0.15 s synchronization allowance and increase invalid geometry events
Test camera plus reconstruction without Motion first; compare valid geometry rate, capture age and synchronization deltas before enabling normal runtime
Do not increase sync/freshness thresholds to hide pairing errors; bounded timestamp matching would require a separate reviewed change if needed
Original intermittent capture timeout may have an independent sensor/SDK cause
